title: Long Way brand system — touchpoint application, guidelines document, and a failed InDesign handoff pivoted to Canva
goal: To continue working on the brand redesign started on previous session
context: Session 2 picks up directly where Session 1 left off — it is explicitly framed as expanding on the previous one, which was left incomplete, and the steps here all deal with applying an already-defined brand system rather than creating it. In this session I’ll be taking an approved system and rolling it out across real-world touchpoints, then documenting and delivering it to the client. And as for whether “always use AI” shaped this choice: it’s close to how I’d already work on a real project, I typically do ask Claude to review work-in-progress against a system, draft supporting copy, and help write documentation, because those are exactly the parts where a second set of eyes catches inconsistencies I’ve gone blind to after hours of production work. The exercise format pushes me to lean on it more consistently and explicitly than I might unprompted.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: it wrote the brand guidelines without mistakes or need for further clarification

Step 1 + Step 3.step_name: Step 1: Apply the system to key touchpoints / Step 3: Draft the brand guidelines content
Step 1 + Step 3.step_action:
Step 1: I design the packaging label, storefront signage, a business card and three social templates using only the tokens from Step 4. I ask Claude to review each application against the system and flag anything off-system, to draft the copy for the social templates, and to generate the platform-specific crops.

Step 3: I ask Claude to propose the page-by-page structure of the guidelines and to draft the body copy for each section — logo usage, clear space and minimum size, misuse, color, typography, imagery, and tone of voice.

nodes.label: Recap session goal and prep assets
nodes.detail: Recaps that session 1 established the Long Way brand system and states today's goal is to apply it to real touchpoints. Exports the logo from Illustrator and confirms the client interview notes and logo are the only assets available to upload.

nodes.label: Upload assets and submit touchpoint prompt
nodes.detail: Uploads the logo and creative-brief PDF to the Claude Cowork 'Long Way' project, selects the Sonnet 5 model at medium effort to conserve credits, and submits a prompt asking Claude to design a packaging label, business card and three social templates using only the Step 4 tokens, excluding signage this time and leaving the logo unmodified.

nodes.label: Read assets and ask clarifying questions
nodes.detail: Claude's Cowork progress tracker reads the creative-brief PDF and the logo.png project file, then pauses to ask a clarifying question: 'What kind of packaging label do you need for Long Way?', offering hang tag/garment label, shipping box/mailer label, or both as options.

nodes.label: Build guideline color and font foundations
nodes.detail: While Claude works, the user builds brand-guideline foundations themselves in Illustrator: finalizing a five-color palette (black, light grey, slate blue, sage green, rust/terracotta) applied next to the logo, and documenting a font pairing (Atelia headline, Futura PT subtitle/body, cursive Beloved Script accent).

nodes.label: Answer Claude's clarifying questions
Deliver combined web-artifact visual system
nodes.detail: Claude's Cowork tracker moves through preparing the logo asset and building the visual system canvas, then delivers a six-artboard combined HTML artifact (system overview, hang tag front/back, business card front/back, three Instagram templates) with Argentine Spanish copy and the palette hex codes (#26301F, #585D5F, #BD5B2C, #DAC9A2, #F4EFE3), and offers to publish it as a hosted link.

nodes.label: Continue working on building guideline color and font foundations
Pull moody reference photography
nodes.detail: Browses Pinterest for moody, weathered Mar del Plata coastline photography (searching 'mar del plata clima') and pulls reference images into a placeholder 'PHOTOGRAPHY' artboard in the same Illustrator file, next to the Atelia/Futura PT font-labeling artboard.

nodes.label: Request editable mockups with specified fonts and colors
nodes.detail: Signals they already has the fonts and colors locked, pushing Claude toward individually editable per-touchpoint files instead.

nodes.label: Deliver seven editable SVG touchpoint mockup files
nodes.detail: Instead of the combined artifact, Claude delivers seven individual editable SVG files matching the requested touchpoints: Hangtag front and back, Businesscard front and back, and three social templates (Social craft, Social product, Social testimonial). Claude confirms type is set to Atelia/Futura PT/Beloved Script by name, the palette was swapped in exactly as sampled (black #DADADA-grey, slate #54717A, sage #C4C490, rust #A05C2E), and the logo is embedded unmodified.

nodes.label: Draft guidelines page structure themselves
nodes.detail: While Claude finishes revising the Step 1 deliverables in the background, the user drafts the page-by-page structure for the brand guidelines document themselves directly in a new Illustrator artboard, typing out a running list: intro page, index, about us, brand story, logo, usages, safe area, color palette and approved contrast applications, fonts and uses, photography, social media, tone of voice, and 8 pages for mockups.

nodes.label: Review the generated seven editable mockup files
nodes.detail: Comments the generated files look nice.

Step 2.step_name: Write and lay out the brand guidelines document
Step 2.step_action: I ask Claude to propose the page-by-page structure of the guidelines and to draft the body copy for each section. Logo usage, clear space and minimum size, misuse, color, typography, imagery, tone of voice. I build the editorial layout in InDesign (grid, running heads, section openers), place the final assets, and export a print- and screen-ready PDF.

nodes.label: Send structure and brand context, request layout
nodes.detail: Sends Claude their drafted page structure along with additional brand context: the handmade-production focus and that the target buyers are tourists caught in the city expecting beach days who end up with bad weather and no jackets in their suitcase. Asks Claude to lay out the full brand guidelines using this content plus an attached photography page.

nodes.label: Read references and produce guideline pages
nodes.detail: Claude works for several minutes, reading in reference photography pages (page09.png, page10.png, page11.png, etc.) and producing and revising more than a dozen individual page files for the 20-page guidelines document, tracked live in the Cowork progress panel.

nodes.label: Request an InDesign-editable file
nodes.detail: Types 'give me an editable file that I can work in InDesign' into Cowork after finding they cannot work directly with the delivered PDF.

nodes.label: Deliver an .idml file with caveats
nodes.detail: Claude delivers an .idml (InDesign Markup) file rather than a native .indd, explaining every graphic element is a placed background image and all 167 text frames (headlines, body text, captions, labels, page numbers) are live editable text frames. Warns InDesign will prompt about missing fonts (Atelia, Futura PT, Beloved Script) and substitute temporarily, and admits it cannot itself test-open the file in InDesign to verify it opens cleanly.

nodes.label: Review delivered 20-page PDF, flag quality problems, and save it to Google Drive
nodes.detail: Reviews the delivered 20-page 'Long way brand guidelines' PDF, paging through the cover, table of contents, color and contrast section, fonts-and-uses page, and mockup section. Flags an unexplained pink color they can't source (appearing repeatedly across pages, including a weird glow), an inappropriate watch/tablet mockup used for a social post that doesn't fit the handmade-jacket brand, and body copy that mixes English and Spanish within the same page.

nodes.label: Prepare to open Claude's delivered file using Adobe InDesign
nodes.detail: Closes their personal Illustrator working file and opens Adobe InDesign.

nodes.label: Download Claude's delivered file and open it in InDesign and discover broken frames
nodes.detail: Opens the delivered file in Adobe InDesign and discovers every page's image frames are broken, empty placeholder boxes instead of the actual photography and graphics, with a live error counter in the status bar (observed around 162-163 and climbing as they page through) reflecting on the order of 167 link/content errors reported across the file. Pages through all 20 pages of the document confirming the same broken-frame problem throughout. Concludes that manually re-linking and rearranging every broken frame across all 20 pages would take way longer than redoing the guidelines from scratch, calls the deliverable 'inviable' out loud.

nodes.label: Ask Claude for a Canva-editable version
nodes.detail: Types 'give me a file that I can edit in Canva' into Cowork.

nodes.label: Explain PPTX approach and warn of font substitution
nodes.detail: Claude explains it built the file as a .pptx rather than a native Canva file, since PowerPoint is what Canva actually imports as an editable design (via Create a design > Import file), preserving the same structure and all 167 text elements as live editable text boxes, rendered through LibreOffice first to confirm the 20 slides lay out correctly. Explicitly warns that Canva will substitute its own fonts for Atelia, Futura PT and Beloved Script since those exact fonts are not in Canva's library, requiring manual replacement after import.

nodes.label: Abandon Claude's previous delivered file, and open Canva to prepare for the incoming Claude's Canva-editable file
nodes.detail: Decides to abandon InDesign editing for the previous Claude delivered file entirely, expressing frustration at the minutes lost waiting for a broken deliverable. Switches to a tool they can reliably edit it themselves, and opens Canva to prepare for the incoming file.

nodes.label: Download Claude's delivered file and open Canva to edit the file
nodes.detail: Abandons the InDesign approach using Claude's delivered file in favor of a tool they can reliably edit it themselves, and opens Canva to prepare for the incoming file.

Step 4.step_name: Lay out and produce the brand guidelines document
Step 4.step_action: I build the editorial layout in InDesign (grid, running heads, section openers), place the final assets from Step 3, and export a print- and screen-ready PDF.

nodes.label: Open PPTX in Canva and fix mixed-language text
nodes.detail: Opens the delivered .pptx file in Canva and manually edits the 'About Us' (Sobre Nosotros) page text, fixing the 'Spanglish' mixing of English and Spanish they flagged earlier so the copy reads consistently in Spanish.

nodes.label: Manually correct fonts and finalize PDF export
nodes.detail: Uses Canva's font search panel to manually reapply the correct typefaces (Atelia, Futura PT, Beloved Script) in place of Canva's automatic font substitutions, going page by page through the 20-slide deck. Reviews the hang-tag mockup page to confirm the front and back tag copy displays consistently in Spanish, finishes reviewing the final pages including the "Papelería — flat lay" mockup, and downloads the corrected, finalized brand guidelines as a PDF.

Step 5.step_name: Package the asset kit and prepare the client handoff
Step 5.step_action: I export the full asset library (logo in .ai/.eps/.svg/.png, color swatch libraries, social templates) and organize it into a folder structure a non-designer can navigate. I ask Claude to write the handoff README documenting every file and its intended use, plus a short client-facing summary email with next steps.

nodes.label: Request README and clarify folder is their own job
nodes.detail: Attaches the finished guidelines PDF in Cowork and asks Claude to create a READ ME / HELP file for the client to read how to use the files, stating they will include it in the final handoff folder themselves — explicitly separating the folder-organizing task (her own job) from the documentation-writing task (Claude's job).

nodes.label: Write the Long Way README
nodes.detail: Delivers a 'Long Way README' PDF, written as one page in Spanish with a top 'what do you need to do?' quick-decision section, then a rundown of every file in the folder (the guidelines PDF, PPTX and IDML versions, the hang tag and business card SVGs, logo.png) with what it's for and what to open it with, a note on the licensed fonts (Atelia, Futura PT, Beloved Script) not being bundled, and the logo's quick-rule cheat sheet.

nodes.label: Download SVGs from Claude and adds the SVGs to the Long Way client folder
Review Claude's README response about and download the file
nodes.detail: Reviews Claude's response about the Write the Long Way README, says that everything is super clear and doesn't need any editing, and downloads the README file.

nodes.label: Move deliverables into the project folder
nodes.detail: Moves the finalized deliverable files, including the new README, into the Long Way project folder in Finder, alongside the SVGs, PPTX, IDML, and logo assets already downloaded.

nodes.label: Build and reorganize the HANDOFF folder
nodes.detail: Builds a 'HANDOFF' folder and, after one round of reorganizing an initial untitled subfolder, settles on 'FOR DIGITAL,' 'FOR PRINTING,' and 'LOGO' subfolders, removing one extra file (an internal working document) they decide isn't meant for the client, to finish the final handoff package alongside the guidelines PDF and README at the folder root.
